This is a NEW simulator microbenchmark, separate from the corrected four-qubit CartPole learning dataset already incorporated. Do not retrain or replace that dataset.

Please integrate an appropriately concise methods/results example, timing table, accuracy limitations and figure into the PQDQN/Pauli-propagation discussion. Update any stale capability claims: PQDQN now supports QASP's differentiable Pauli engine via device="lightning.pp", diff_method="backprop". This is QASP's backend selector, not an upstream PennyLane Lightning device plugin. Current implementation/docs: qasp/rl/qfunctions/models.py, qasp/rl/differentiable_pp_sim.py, docs/qfunctions.md. Gradients flow to circuit/input-scaling/head parameters; arbitrary batches are evaluated sample by sample. Do not promise fast or accurate learning from approximate gradients.

Setup: ten qubits, four YZ AngleAnsatz layers, trainable Y encoding with tanh inputs and reuploading, ring CNOTs including final layer; ten shared Z_i expectations followed by a biased two-output affine head, Q=Wz+b. 142 trainable parameters. Five matched initial parameter seeds 7-11, QASP normal_0_1 initializer = N(0,1), not standard deviation .1. Identical saved parameters and normal input tensors for each backend. CPU float64; sequential samples for both; one Torch intra/inter-op and OMP/OpenBLAS/MKL thread. Apple M1, 16 GiB, eight hardware cores; Python3.13.3, Torch2.14.1, PennyLane0.45.1, Lightning0.45.0.
Baseline lightning.qubit/adjoint; PP k=2 and k=3, pp_prune=False, pp_topM=None, pp_tau=0 (ONLY Pauli-weight truncation, no coefficient pruning).
Two warmups then seven repeats for each seed/backend/batch/workload; shuffled backend order within each repeat. Times below are mean +/- sample SD of FIVE within-seed medians, in milliseconds per complete batch (not confidence intervals).

Batch1:
lightning.qubit inference 26.9023 +/- 7.4354; forward+backward 28.5919 +/- 5.4532.
PP k2 inference 13.8897 +/- 4.2738; forward+backward 16.6931 +/- 1.8672.
PP k3 inference 30.8659 +/- 8.1460; forward+backward 48.2437 +/- 10.1194.
Batch8:
lightning.qubit inference 190.4734 +/- 27.7083; forward+backward 198.0167 +/- 9.0036.
PP k2 inference 83.1824 +/- 7.5301; forward+backward 110.2882 +/- 8.1608.
PP k3 inference 215.6600 +/- 28.7367; forward+backward 326.9149 +/- 30.3535.

Forward+backward includes zero_grad, PQDQN forward, selected-action mean SmoothL1Loss and backward. Fixed alternating actions, targets linspace(.25,1.75); excludes optimizer, environment, replay, target-network evaluations. It is NOT a full DQN step or a learning curve.

Critical accuracy findings (batch8 means across seeds):
k2 feature RMSE .0316434, Q RMSE .0176346, feature relative L2 .9983931, quantum-gradient relative L2 1.0001797, quantum-gradient cosine -.0151345.
k3 feature RMSE .0316141, Q RMSE .0175463, feature relative L2 .9972956, quantum-gradient relative L2 .9991267, quantum-gradient cosine .0372123.
Quantum gradients include circuit rotations + input scales, exclude head. Relative error = norm(g_PP-g_exact)/norm(g_exact). Both cutoffs yield poor approximations despite small absolute Q errors: shared bias/head can obscure quantum-feature loss. k2 is ~1.80x faster for this batch8 gradient workload, k3 is slower than exact Lightning. NO claim of equivalent/faster RL learning, accuracy-preserving speedup, scalability, or universal superiority. One local session, no core pinning/thermal control, five parameter seeds are not five independent machine sessions.
